title: A separate AJAX controller for every backend feature
today: Each controller parses arguments, validates them and formats errors in a different way.
solution: A generic dispatcher handles all actions. TYPO3 validates arguments and results against a schema from the method signature.

title: No general-purpose API in the core
today: Integrations depend on extensions, and each extension builds and maintains separate endpoints.
solution: Every action of TYPO3 or of an extension has an HTTP endpoint below `/typo3/api/`.

title: Separate authorization for every integration
today: Each integration builds API keys, OAuth and fine-grained permissions again.
solution: EXT:hub offers OAuth 2.0 and static tokens. Scopes limit apps, and the permissions of the user always apply.

title: No machine-readable description
today: Developers document endpoints by hand, if at all, and over time the documentation and the code differ.
solution: TYPO3 generates an OpenAPI 3.1 document from the code. Swagger UI shows the document.

title: No standard interface for AI agents
today: Assistants have no safe, standard way to read or change content for an editor.
solution: The built-in MCP server offers actions as tools. Agents act as the user, and the granted scopes limit the agents.

title: Glue code for every consumer
today: The backend UI, integrations and automation each need separate glue code.
solution: Developers implement a feature once, as an action, and every channel can use the action.
